outputs.L1: The invention relates to a system for monitoring the position of the closing unit of an injection-molding machine by bypassing a light curtain that serves to secure the closing unit and the tool area of the injection-molding machine. The injection-molding machine comprises at least one molding tool consisting of at least two parts, the tool enclosing at least one mold cavity. The injection-molding machine further comprises a programmable logic controller (PLC) for controlling the movement monitoring module (MOC) for indirect position monitoring of the closing unit and of the position of the molding tool parts relative to one another. Distance-measuring rods are provided as sensors, the signals of which are processed in the PLC via the MOC. After the closing pressure has been built up and the mold has been filled, the tool parts must maintain a spacing gap relative to one another during the subsequent bumping step, the gap being assigned a specific maximum value. If this value is exceeded, the injection-molding machine shuts off.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a system for supervising the position of the clamping or closing unit in an injection-molding machine while bypassing a light curtain used to protect the closing unit and the tool region of the machine. The injection-molding machine includes at least one molding tool made up of at least two sections, and this tool surrounds at least one mold cavity. The machine is equipped with a programmable logic controller (PLC), which controls a movement monitoring module (MOC) for indirectly monitoring both the position of the closing unit and the relative positions of the molding-tool sections. Distance-measuring rods are used as sensors, and their signals are evaluated in the PLC through the MOC. After the closing pressure has been generated and the mold has been filled, the tool sections must remain separated from one another by a spacing gap during the following bumping operation. This gap is assigned a defined maximum permissible value, and the injection-molding machine is switched off if that value is exceeded.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a system for monitoring the position of the closing unit of an injection-molding machine, particularly in operating situations in which a protective light curtain is bypassed or temporarily rendered ineffective. The system is intended to ensure that the closing unit and the molding tool remain in a safe and controlled position, even when normal protective monitoring by the light curtain is not available.

The injection-molding machine comprises a molding tool having at least two tool parts. These tool parts are movable relative to one another and, in the closed state, enclose at least one mold cavity into which molding material can be injected. Correct positioning of the tool parts is essential both for the quality of the molded product and for the safe operation of the machine.

A programmable logic controller is provided for controlling and monitoring the machine operation. The programmable logic controller controls a movement monitoring module, which is used for indirect position monitoring of the closing unit. Through this movement monitoring module, the system also monitors the relative positions of the individual molding tool parts. In this way, the actual movement and position of the closing unit can be supervised without relying solely on the protective light curtain.

Distance measuring sticks are used as sensors for detecting the relative position or spacing of the tool parts. These sensors generate signals corresponding to the measured distance or movement. The signals are supplied to the programmable logic controller and are processed there by means of the movement monitoring module. Based on these signals, the controller can determine whether the closing unit and the tool parts are within the permitted positional range.

A particularly important monitoring function is performed during the bumping step. During this step, the tool parts must maintain a spacing gap that remains below a predefined maximum value. This maximum spacing value represents a safety limit. If the measured gap between the tool parts exceeds the specified maximum value, the programmable logic controller initiates a shutdown of the injection-molding machine. This prevents unsafe machine operation and reduces the risk of injury or damage while the protective light curtain is bypassed.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a safety and monitoring system for an injection-molding machine, in particular for monitoring the closing unit and the relative position of mold tool parts when a protective light curtain is temporarily bypassed during operation.

In injection-molding machines, the mold tool is typically arranged in a closing unit having at least one movable platen and one fixed platen. During the production cycle, the movable platen is displaced relative to the fixed platen in order to open and close the mold. For safety reasons, the working area of the closing unit is commonly protected by guards, protective doors, or light curtains. However, in certain operating modes or process steps, it may be necessary to bypass or mute the protective light curtain, for example during a bumping step or during specific mold-related movements after pressure buildup and filling. In such situations, additional monitoring is required to ensure that no hazardous machine movement or excessive opening of the mold occurs.

The invention provides an indirect position-monitoring arrangement for this purpose. Instead of relying solely on direct position feedback from the drive system of the closing unit, one or more distance-measuring sensors are arranged so that they detect a distance associated with the position of the closing unit and/or the mold tool parts. These sensors may be positioned to measure the spacing between machine components, between platens, or between reference surfaces connected to the mold halves. The measured distance values are supplied as sensor signals to a programmable logic controller, in particular to a PLC movement-monitoring module configured for safety-related evaluation.

The PLC movement-monitoring module processes the sensor signals and determines whether the mold tool parts remain within an allowable relative position range. In particular, the system monitors whether a defined maximum spacing gap between the mold parts is maintained. This is especially relevant during the bumping step following pressure buildup and filling of the mold cavity. During this step, a slight relative movement or spacing may be permitted, but the gap must not exceed a predetermined maximum value. The maximum permissible spacing can be stored as a parameter in the PLC and may be adapted to the specific mold, material, or production process.

If the distance-measuring sensors indicate that the actual gap between the mold parts is equal to or below the defined maximum spacing, the machine may continue operating in the intended mode even while the protective light curtain is bypassed. If, however, the evaluated distance exceeds the permissible gap, the PLC movement-monitoring module generates a safety signal. This signal causes the injection-molding machine to be stopped, the closing unit drive to be disabled, or another predefined safe state to be initiated. In this way, the system prevents dangerous opening movements or unintended mold separation during a phase in which ordinary access protection is not fully active.

The invention therefore improves operational safety by providing an independent or supplementary monitoring function for the mold position. By using distance-measuring sensors in combination with safety-oriented PLC evaluation, the position of the mold parts can be monitored indirectly and reliably without requiring direct measurement at the mold cavity itself. The arrangement allows necessary process steps to be carried out while the protective light curtain is bypassed, but only under controlled conditions in which the mold parts remain within a safe, predefined spacing range.

As a result, the injection-molding machine can perform the required bumping operation after pressure buildup and filling while maintaining a high level of safety. Any deviation beyond the defined maximum gap is detected quickly and leads to automatic shutdown or transition into a safe operating state. This reduces the risk of injury to operating personnel and prevents unsafe machine conditions, while still allowing efficient and flexible execution of the molding process.
outputs.L5:
The PLC and MOC are important concepts in modern industrial operations.

A PLC, or Programmable Logic Controller, is a digital control system used to automate machinery, production lines, and industrial processes. The PLC receives information from sensors, processes it according to programmed logic, and then sends commands to devices such as motors, valves, pumps, and alarms. Because PLCs are reliable, flexible, and designed for harsh environments, they are widely used in manufacturing, energy, water treatment, and many other industries.

MOC, or Management of Change, is a structured process used to control modifications in equipment, procedures, software, or operating conditions. The purpose of MOC is to ensure that any change is reviewed, approved, documented, and implemented safely. When a PLC program is updated, for example, the MOC process helps identify possible risks, confirm that safety systems remain effective, and make sure operators are properly informed and trained.

Together, the PLC and MOC play a key role in maintaining safe and efficient operations. The PLC provides automation and control, while MOC ensures that changes to the system are managed responsibly. By combining strong technical systems with disciplined change management, organizations can reduce downtime, improve safety, and support long-term operational reliability.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention about monitoring the closing unit position in an injection-molding machine using PLC/MOC processing and distance measuring rods, including a shutdown if the mold gap exceeds a maximum during bumping.
counterfactuals.output: An injection-molding machine includes a closing unit having relatively movable mold platens and at least one distance measuring rod arranged to generate position signals representative of a spacing or mold gap between the platens. The position signals are supplied to a control system including a programmable logic controller and/or machine or motion controller processing unit configured to continuously determine an actual closing-unit position during closing, opening, and bumping operation of the mold. During a bumping cycle, the control system compares the detected mold gap with a stored maximum permissible gap value. If the actual mold gap exceeds the maximum permissible value, the control system automatically interrupts the bumping operation and initiates a machine shutdown or safety stop. The monitoring arrangement thereby provides direct position supervision of the closing unit, improves protection of the mold and machine components, and permits reliable detection of abnormal platen separation during controlled mold movements.
